expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "there's a window where old pods/instances (still running the code that reads legacy_email) can hit the DB after the column is already gone — that's a live error"

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "Ship the code-only change today... Run the DROP COLUMN as its own deploy, separately."

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "The DROP COLUMN is the irreversible step. The restore path is 'point-in-time recovery / a full backup restore'"

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "The code-only deploy has a two-minute rollback (revert). The drop does not" and "your rollback is a DB restore, on a weekend, with reduced coverage"

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "if you drop it at 4pm Friday and something unexpected reads it, your rollback is a DB restore, on a weekend, with reduced coverage"

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: "a CI guard that blocks DROP/destructive ALTER from landing in the same PR as app code, so this split becomes automatic going forward"

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "Green CI and passing tests don't cover this, because tests don't exercise 'old code, new schema' during a rolling deploy"

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: "This part is fully reversible (git revert + redeploy)" for code changes vs DROP COLUMN as irreversible
